# The status checks the `main` branch ruleset requires, one per line.
#
# ⚠️ THIS FILE EXISTS BECAUSE THE RULESET DOES NOT LIVE IN THIS REPOSITORY.
# It is GitHub repository settings, editable in a browser, versioned by nothing.
# The coupling it creates is the sharpest edge in CI:
#
#   ci.yml generates a check NAME  ->  the ruleset requires that exact string
#
# Rename a job, or change a matrix value, and the required check is never
# reported. GitHub does not treat a missing required check as passed — it waits
# for it forever, so every pull request becomes unmergeable, and nothing in the
# repository says why. `full stack on kind (full)` and `(lite)` are especially
# exposed, because the matrix value is interpolated INTO the name.
#
# Splitting that unverifiable coupling into two verifiable halves is the whole
# point of this file:
#
#   1. scripts/check-doc-claims.py asserts every line below is a name ci.yml can
#      actually produce. Offline, on every run, so a rename fails in the same
#      pull request that made it.
#   2. the `settings-drift` job asserts this file matches the LIVE ruleset. That
#      needs the network, so it runs weekly rather than per-pull-request. It
#      catches the other direction: someone editing the ruleset in the browser.
#
# Neither half needs the other to be useful. Together they cover workflow ->
# settings -> prose.
#
# ⚠️ ADDING A LINE HERE DOES NOT MAKE A CHECK REQUIRED. This file is a record,
# not a control plane. Change the ruleset first, then record it here, or
# settings-drift will tell you they disagree — which is exactly its job.
#
# ⚠️ THREE JOBS THAT ENCODE THIS REPO'S CENTRAL CLAIMS ARE NOT REQUIRED, and that has
# never been written down as a decision. `helm chart (lint, render, assertions fire)` —
# the job whose entire purpose is driving every render-time assertion to its FAILURE —
# plus `compose stack (no Kubernetes)` and `simulator image (build both arches,
# smoke-test amd64)` can all be red on a pull request that merges. CodeQL's advisory
# status is argued at length in codeql.yml; these three are not mentioned anywhere.
#
# NOT FIXED BY ADDING THEM HERE. This file is a record, not a control plane — the note
# above says so, and adding a line the ruleset does not carry makes `settings-drift`
# report a disagreement, correctly. Change the ruleset in the browser FIRST, then add
# the three names below. Until someone does, this paragraph is the record that it was
# considered rather than overlooked.
#
# The ruleset: https://github.com/ChrisAdkin8/k8s-ai-observability/settings/rules

selftest + rule tests + shell syntax
full stack on kind (full)
full stack on kind (lite)
chart on kind (helm test, foreign Prometheus)
